project.name: Windows Copilot API
project.description: A free LLM API powered by Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI-compatible. Turns the free chat at copilot.microsoft.com into an API you can call from code.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package init that re-exports the public API classes (CopilotClient, ChatReply, Copilot, ClearanceRequired, BrowserCopilot, load_auth) from the copilot submodules.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel file; imports and re-exports are the only contents.

nodes.name: auth.py
nodes.summary: Manages signed-in session caching for the pure-HTTP path, loading and refreshing cookies and MSAL access tokens from a browser profile or cached snapshot.

nodes.name: load_auth
nodes.summary: Returns signed-in cookies and access token from cache or by launching a headless/visible browser session to refresh them.

nodes.name: browser.py
nodes.summary: Drives Playwright for Copilot sign-in, Cloudflare Turnstile clearance, and chat token capture, enabling headless session refresh for the pure-HTTP driver.

nodes.name: BrowserCopilot
nodes.summary: Launches a persistent Playwright Chromium profile to handle interactive sign-in, headless chat token capture via WebSocket, and Cloudflare Turnstile bypass for the Copilot session.
nodes.languageNotes: 28 methods; uses Playwright sync API with persistent context for session reuse across runs.

nodes.name: 01_direct_chat.py
nodes.summary: Demonstrates the simplest in-process chat usage of CopilotClient with a single non-streaming reply.

nodes.name: 02_direct_conversation.py
nodes.summary: Demonstrates multi-turn conversation by reusing conversation_id to continue a Copilot chat session.

nodes.name: 03_direct_stream.py
nodes.summary: Demonstrates streaming Copilot chat responses incrementally as they are generated.

nodes.name: challenges.py
nodes.summary: Proof-of-work challenge solvers for Copilot's chat WebSocket, implementing hashcash and arithmetic copilot variants that mirror copilot.microsoft.com's own client.

nodes.name: _hashcash_ok
nodes.summary: Checks whether a SHA-256 digest has at least a given number of leading zero bits for hashcash proof-of-work validation.

nodes.name: solve_hashcash
nodes.summary: Solves a hashcash challenge by finding the smallest nonce whose SHA-256 digest has the required leading zero bits.

nodes.name: solve_copilot_challenge
nodes.summary: Solves the arithmetic copilot challenge by computing floor((a^3/100 + a*25) mod 22) rounded to nearest integer.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: High-level Copilot client providing chat and stream methods with transparent auth refresh, Cloudflare clearance recovery via browser, and anonymous mode support.

nodes.name: _status
nodes.summary: Emits a progress or recovery message to stderr so it never mixes into reply text on stdout.

nodes.name: ChatReply
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the full result of a chat call, including text, conversation id, and any generated images.

nodes.name: ChatStream
nodes.summary: Iterable stream of reply chunks that also exposes the conversation id, yielding text and ImageResponse items.

nodes.name: CopilotClient
nodes.summary: Main Copilot client managing signed-in auth, Cloudflare clearance recovery, and chat/stream interactions across multiple conversations.

nodes.name: driver.py
nodes.summary: Pure-HTTP Copilot driver implementing Microsoft's consumer chat protocol over a Cloudflare-impersonating curl_cffi session with WebSocket streaming and in-process challenge solving.

nodes.name: ClearanceRequired
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the chat socket demands a Cloudflare Turnstile token that cannot be minted in a pure-HTTP session.

nodes.name: Copilot

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what this project does: it turns the free Microsoft Copilot chat into an OpenAI-compatible API you can call from code. It works both as a Python library (CopilotClient) and a local server at localhost:8000/v1 that speaks the OpenAI format, so the official openai SDK works as a drop-in replacement.

tour.title: Server Entry Point
tour.description: app.py is the top-level script that launches the server. It imports server/__init__.py, which wires up uvicorn on a configurable host/port and ensures a Copilot auth session exists before serving requests. This is where the application transitions from a Python module into a running HTTP service.

tour.title: API Router & Handlers
tour.description: server/api.py is the heart of the OpenAI-compatible server — a FastAPI application with routes for listing models and generating chat completions. The chat_completions handler validates requests, enforces rate limits, then dispatches to either a streaming generator or a non-streaming completion builder. This file ties together all the server submodules.

tour.title: OpenAI Format Translation
tour.description: Building on the API router, these three modules handle the protocol translation. server/schemas.py defines Pydantic models for OpenAI's chat completion request shape. server/openai_format.py builds OpenAI-compliant response dicts and SSE streaming chunks. server/prompt.py flattens the OpenAI messages array (system messages, multi-turn history, content parts) into the single prompt string Copilot expects.

tour.title: Rate Limiting & Configuration
tour.description: server/ratelimit.py implements a token-bucket rate limiter that enforces a self-imposed ceiling on upstream requests to Microsoft Copilot. server/config.py reads environment variables for the model name, rate limit RPM, and burst size, providing sensible defaults. Together they protect both the upstream service and the local server from overload.

tour.title: Copilot Client SDK
tour.description: The copilot package barrel (copilot/__init__.py) re-exports the public API. The main class, CopilotClient in copilot/client.py, provides high-level chat() and stream() methods that abstract away authentication, Cloudflare clearance recovery, and conversation management. This is what the API server calls internally and what Python library users import directly.

tour.title: Protocol Driver & Challenge Solving
tour.description: copilot/driver.py implements the pure-HTTP Copilot provider over a Cloudflare-impersonating curl_cffi session. It handles conversation creation, attachment upload, WebSocket handshake, and streaming response parsing. copilot/protocol.py stores the WebSocket URL, handshake frames, and consent constants captured from a live session. copilot/challenges.py solves the hashcash and arithmetic proof-of-work challenges Microsoft requires before allowing chat.

tour.title: Authentication & Browser Automation
tour.description: copilot/auth.py manages signed-in session caching: it stores cookies and MSAL access tokens from a browser profile, and refreshes them automatically when they expire. copilot/browser.py drives Playwright for interactive sign-in, headless Cloudflare Turnstile clearance via WebSocket intercept, and chat token capture. Together they keep the session alive without user intervention.

tour.title: Shared Data Models & Utilities
tour.description: copilot/models.py defines the data types shared across both the pure-HTTP and browser paths: ImageResponse, the AbstractProvider base class, and the thread-safe Conversation container. copilot/utils.py provides low-level helpers — HTTP status checking, WebSocket JSON frame reassembly via drain_json, and image encoding utilities for attachment upload.

tour.title: Containerization & Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the application based on the Playwright Python image (which ships Chromium preinstalled), installs dependencies, and serves the API on port 8000. docker-compose.yml adds port mapping, rate-limit environment variables, and a bind-mounted session volume for persistent browser profile storage across restarts, making it trivial to deploy anywhere Docker runs.
